holidays.name: National Bittersweet Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the complex, slightly bitter, slightly sweet chocolate that grown-ups pretend to love while secretly wishing it were milk chocolate. Dark chocolate fans nibble squares, bake brownies, and debate cacao percentages.
holidays.origin: A food observance that appears on unofficial holiday calendars, created by chocolate enthusiasts and food-calendar compilers. It has no single known founder, which is typical for many American food days.
holidays.funFact: Bittersweet chocolate generally contains at least 35% cacao by U.S. standards, but many bars boast 60% or more. Cacao seeds were once used as currency by the Aztecs.

holidays.name: Houseplant Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the leafy roommates who silently judge your life choices. Celebrants water, dust, repot, and talk lovingly to their ferns, succulents, and that one fiddle-leaf fig that refuses to thrive.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance popularized by gardening communities and plant lovers, timed for the dreary winter stretch when outdoor gardens are dormant and indoor greenery matters most.
holidays.funFact: NASA research in the 1980s found that some houseplants can help remove certain airborne toxins in sealed chambers, though a typical home would need a jungle's worth of plants to make a big difference.

holidays.name: Bird Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to our feathered friends, encouraging people to put out feeders, go birdwatching, and learn why a pigeon is secretly a majestic creature. Expect a lot of binoculars and whispered excitement over a sparrow.
holidays.origin: Bird Day was proposed in 1894 by Charles Almanzo Babcock, a Pennsylvania school superintendent, as a way to teach children about bird conservation. It later spread through schools and conservation groups across the United States.
holidays.funFact: Babcock's original Bird Day was meant as a school-based alternative to Arbor Day, and it was among the earliest bird-focused awareness efforts in America.

holidays.name: Peculiar People Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace the oddballs, weirdos, and wonderfully strange people in your life, including yourself. Wear the mismatched socks, share the unusual hobby, and celebrate everyone who marches to their own drum.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew out of calendars of offbeat holidays, encouraging people to appreciate individuality and eccentricity rather than conformity.
holidays.funFact: The word peculiar comes from the Latin 'peculiaris,' meaning 'of one's own property,' so being peculiar originally meant something was uniquely your own.

holidays.name: Save the Eagles Day
holidays.description: A day to honor and protect eagles, the soaring symbols of freedom that are also very good at stealing fish from other birds. Wildlife fans celebrate recovery efforts and promote habitat conservation.
holidays.origin: An awareness observance tied to wildlife conservation groups, highlighting the dramatic comeback of bald eagles after near extinction from habitat loss and pesticide use like DDT.
holidays.funFact: Bald eagles build some of the largest nests of any North American bird, with some weighing over a ton and being used for decades.
